dlsym_scope.fact: Handle-scoped dlsym searches the specified object and objects automatically loaded with it in dependency order; global/default lookup and preload interposition are distinct loader mechanisms.

grf.observed_anchor: PR #555 uses _sqlite3-handle dlsym(sqlite3_libversion) plus dladdr, exact expected version/path/hash and a Python sqlite3.sqlite_version cross-check; it explicitly does not claim productive persistence.
grf.generated_reality: The handle-scoped symbol-origin probe may still identify the admitted dependency libsqlite3 while actual _sqlite3 calls are interposed by a globally preloaded object.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: If loader symbol resolution for the module and handle-scoped dlsym are inseparable in the tested environment, preload treatment should change the observed dlsym origin or otherwise make the candidate fail closed before productive call divergence.
grf.falsifier: Use one disposable LD_PRELOAD interposition experiment and compare handle-scoped dlsym/dladdr identity with actual Python SQLite call behavior.
grf.collapse: REJECT productive-call binding as a general inference from handle-scoped sqlite3_libversion origin alone. RETAIN PR #555 as scoped dependency-tree symbol-origin evidence.

exactly_one_unusual_experiment.interpretation: A handle-scoped sqlite3_libversion origin can remain pinned to the real dependency libsqlite3 while other SQLite API calls from the process are globally interposed.

architecture_delta.new_invariant: Do not promote productive SQLite call binding from mapped-library identity or _sqlite3-handle sqlite3_libversion symbol-origin identity alone. Accepted ProductStart evidence must additionally bind or fail-close unexpected dynamic-loader interposition state, or provide an equivalent direct relocation/call-path integrity mechanism, together with the real UnifiedDB transaction.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: A production service may already execute in a sanitized loader environment where LD_PRELOAD/audit-style interposition is structurally unreachable; if machine-checked and bound to ProductStart, a separate relocation attestor may be unnecessary.
